milestone.title: mp multi-lane path + status snapshot + kinds simplification

intent.outcome: mp path computes and shows ordered work across 4 lanes (execution default, review, grooming, backlog); mp status gives a snapshot rollup; non-milestone work simplifies to one backlog collection (tweaks+bugs+ideas) with priority tiers. mp next defaults to the execution lane with --lane for others. Plain mp path = execution lane (what an executor needs 90% of the time). Builds on the lifecycle (M100) and findings/remediation (M101).

problem.description: mp path today is a flat topological list of every milestone id (execution-only, milestone-only, single-role). mp status scatters counts. Tracks (BF-/TW-) are a separate collection from backlog, adding kinds complexity. Agents reach for python3/jq because there is no per-lane 'what's next'. The lifecycle (M100) and findings (M101) now provide the states to compute lanes against, and remediation/priority-escalation (M101) feed the review lane.

in_scope: mp path: 4 lanes — execution (milestones by dep DAG + priority tiebreak + id tiebreak), review (milestones by review phase: needs-self-check / awaiting-independent / needs-remediation), grooming (milestones at draft/groomed by dep DAG), backlog (tweaks+bugs+ideas by priority: high → regular-chronological → low/ideas)
mp path default = execution lane; --all shows all 4; --lane <name> selects; --summary gives per-lane counts + total effort where available
mp next = execution lane head; --lane <name> for other lanes
mp status = snapshot rollup (lane counts + blockers + validate + health); distinct from path (ordering)

Kinds simplification: merge tracks (BF-/TW-) into backlog as kind:tweak|bug; ideas become kind:idea with priority low; backlog item priority high/regular/low; migration script (existing items → kind:bug)
Backlog lane ordering: high first, then regular chronological, then low/ideas last; ideas strippable via --no-ideas / --kind
JSON lane schema: each lane declares item_type (step|milestone|backlog-item) so consumers do not assume uniformity

design_decisions.choice: path includes a backlog lane (not milestones-only) because backlog items now have an ordering rule (priority)
design_decisions.rationale: Earlier 'milestones-only' was because only milestones had edges. With priority tiers, backlog earns an ordering; the rule becomes 'path = anything with an ordering rule'.

design_decisions.choice: Collapse tracks into backlog as kind:tweak|bug|idea; ideas are the low-priority tier, not a separate lane
design_decisions.rationale: One queue with priority tiers (high/regular/low) is simpler than two lanes; ideas stay strippable. Existing items migrate to kind:bug for simplicity (no backcompat concern).

design_decisions.choice: Milestone priority (high/regular/low) is a tiebreak within dep topology; id is the final tiebreak among same-priority same-state milestones
design_decisions.rationale: Deps dominate (cannot do M98 before M97); priority breaks ties among ready milestones; creation order (id) is the stable final tiebreak.

findings.description: AC-05 says 'mp path --lane backlog orders high → regular-chronological → low(ideas); --no-ideas strips ideas'. The 'regular-chronological' ordering is not pinned — chronological by what? created date? updated date? backlog.json insertion order? backlog_lane at path_engine.rs:730 uses created/updated but the priority tier ordering within 'regular' is ambiguous. Tighten the AC: 'regular tier ordered by milestone created ascending; if absent, by id ascending; documented in MP-COMMANDS.md path section'.

findings.description: External review 2026-07-05 ER-3: mp next --lane <X> resolves the lane by POSITIONAL index into report.lanes[0..3], hard-coupling the enum arm order to build_lanes' vec![execution,review,grooming,backlog] ordering. status.rs:99-102. Panics at runtime if a lane is conditionally omitted, reordered, or a fifth lane inserted. cmd_path (commands/path.rs:23) already does the safer thing — filters by name and bails on miss. Fix: look up by name (report.lanes.iter().find(|l| l.name == lane_name).ok_or_else(...)).
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: External review 2026-07-05 ER-4: emitted 'lane' JSON field produced via format!('{lane_arg:?}').to_lowercase() — relies on derived Debug of LaneArg to produce 'execution' etc. status.rs:107,116. Rename Backlog → BacklogLane (or any casing change) and the wire format silently drifts, breaking raul M103 consumers. The Lane struct already carries name: String as source of truth. Fix: emit target.name.clone().
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: External review 2026-07-05 ER-5: mp next --summary (without --lane) silently ignores the summary flag — the else branch in cmd_next_step never reads the summary parameter. Only --lane X --summary honors it. A user running --summary gets the full legacy payload with no signal it was a no-op. Fix: honor --summary in the legacy branch, or document that --summary requires --lane (clap requires('lane')).
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: External review 2026-07-05 ER-6: total_effort hardcoded to '—' with 'M102-stretch goal' comment (path_engine.rs:529). Always-present-always-empty in the wire format — a smell for consumers (raul M103 sees a string that is never useful). AC-07 wording '(+ milestone effort rollup where available)' makes this technically conformant. Fix: omit via #[serde(skip_serializing_if)] until implemented, or compute from milestone effort (S/M/L → story points).
findings.author: external-review
